disclaimer.metaDescription: Important information about the educational nature of this website, the off-label use of ketamine, and the limits of what's offered here.
disclaimer.heading: Disclaimer

sections.heading: Educational information only
paragraphs: The content on this website is provided for general educational purposes only. It is not medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment, and it is not a substitute for the guidance of a qualified health provider. Never disregard professional medical advice, or delay seeking it, because of something you have read here.

sections.heading: Off-label use
paragraphs: Ketamine is FDA-approved as an anesthetic. Its use for depression, anxiety, PTSD, and other mental health conditions is "off-label." Off-label prescribing is legal and common when supported by sound medical evidence, but it means these uses have not been formally approved by the FDA for that purpose.

sections.heading: No guarantee of outcome
paragraphs: Ketamine-assisted therapy is a relatively new and still developing intervention. While research is encouraging, individual results vary and no specific outcome is promised or guaranteed. Benefits are generally most durable as part of an overall treatment program.

sections.heading: No therapeutic relationship
paragraphs: Using this website or contacting us through it does not create a therapist–client or provider–patient relationship. Any such relationship begins only after a formal consultation, assessment, and agreement to treatment.

sections.heading: Not a crisis service
paragraphs: This website and its contact form are not monitored around the clock and are not a crisis or emergency service. If you are in crisis or thinking about harming yourself, call or text 988 (U.S.), or dial 911 for emergencies.

privacy.metaDescription: How A World Within handles the limited information collected through this website.
privacy.heading: Privacy Policy

sections.heading: What we collect
paragraphs: This website collects only the information you choose to submit through the consultation request form — your name, email address, optional phone number, and message. We ask that you do not include sensitive health information in that form.

sections.heading: How we use it
paragraphs: We use the information you provide solely to respond to your inquiry and, if appropriate, to schedule a consultation. We do not sell your information or share it with third parties for marketing.

sections.heading: Form processing
paragraphs: Form submissions are processed by our hosting provider (Netlify) and delivered to us by email. Their handling of submitted data is governed by their own privacy practices.

sections.heading: Health information
paragraphs: Any protected health information gathered as part of actual treatment is handled separately, under the confidentiality protections that apply to medical and therapy records — not through this website.

sections.heading: Your choices
paragraphs: You may request that we delete the information you submitted through this site at any time by contacting us at the email address on our contact page.

paragraphs: The site is provided for general information about non-ordinary states of consciousness. It does not provide medical advice and does not create a provider–patient relationship. Please see our Disclaimer for details.

sections.heading: External links
paragraphs: This site may link to third-party resources for your convenience. We are not responsible for the content or practices of those sites.

sections.heading: Changes

informedConsent.metaDescription: Key information about ketamine-assisted therapy — its benefits, risks, side effects, eligibility, alternatives, and the voluntary nature of participation.
informedConsent.heading: Informed Consent & Participation Agreement
informedConsent.intro: This agreement is designed to create clarity, respect, and shared understanding between the Participant and the Integration Facilitator. The intention of this support is to provide a grounded, compassionate, and respectful space for individuals who are exploring, experiencing, or integrating non-ordinary states of consciousness.
informedConsent.callout:
This page is educational. Before you begin, you'll review and sign a complete informed-consent document with Becky, and you'll have the chance to ask anything you wish. It's very important to us that you feel safe and respected throughout.

Participation is a personal choice. You are invited to engage with curiosity, self-responsibility, and awareness of your own needs, values, and boundaries.
informedConsent.reviewNote: A complete, signed consent document is provided during your intake, and you'll have the chance to ask about anything in it.

sections.heading: Understanding This Support
paragraphs:
Preparation, non-ordinary state support, and integration support may include:
•	Conversations intended to help you clarify intentions, expectations, hopes, concerns, and personal boundaries.
•	Support in developing practices for grounding, reflection, and self-awareness.
•	Presence and compassionate support during experiences involving non-ordinary states of consciousness.
•	Opportunities to explore meaning, insights, emotions, memories, sensations, or perspectives that may arise.
•	Support in reflecting on experiences afterward and considering how they may relate to your life, relationships, values, or personal growth.
The Integration Facilitator does not direct, control, interpret, or define your experience. Your experience belongs to you.

sections.heading: Your Role as Participant
paragraphs:
You understand that you are an active participant in this process. You are responsible for:
•	Making your own decisions regarding your participation.
•	Communicating your needs, boundaries, questions, and concerns.
•	Providing accurate information that may affect your safety and experience.
•	Seeking additional resources or professional support when you determine it is needed.
•	Taking responsibility for choices related to substances, practices, environments, and personal wellbeing.
You may pause, decline, or discontinue participation at any time.

sections.heading: Role of the Integration Facilitator
paragraphs:
The Integration Facilitator’s role is to offer preparation, presence, support, reflection, and integration assistance.
The Integration Facilitator does not:
•	Diagnose, treat, or cure medical or mental health conditions.
•	Guarantee specific outcomes or experiences.
•	Provide medical advice.
•	Make decisions for the Participant.
•	Represent this support as licensed healthcare, psychotherapy, or medical treatment.
•	Replace emergency, medical, psychiatric, or therapeutic care when those services are appropriate.

sections.heading: Benefits & Risks
paragraphs: Non-ordinary states of consciousness can have positive effects when they happen in safe and healthy ways. For example, meditation, deep prayer, creative flow, and dreaming can help people feel calmer, reduce stress, and gain new insights about themselves. Some people find that these experiences improve their creativity, emotional healing, or sense of connection with others. When practiced responsibly, these states can support personal growth, self-awareness, and overall well-being.

Non-ordinary states of consciousness can also have risks, especially when they are caused by alcohol, drugs, sleep deprivation, or unsafe situations. These states may affect judgment, memory, and decision-making, increasing the chance of accidents or risky behavior. Some people may experience fear, confusion, anxiety, or emotional distress, and those with certain mental health conditions may be more vulnerable to negative effects. Understanding these risks and making safe choices can help reduce harm while supporting both physical and mental health.

sections.heading: Non-Ordinary States of Consciousness
paragraphs:
Non-ordinary states of consciousness can be meaningful, challenging, unfamiliar, inspiring, confusing, or transformative. Experiences may vary widely from person to person.
A Participant may experience a range of emotional, physical, cognitive, perceptual, or spiritual experiences, including but not limited to:
•	Heightened awareness or sensitivity
•	Strong emotions
•	Memories or personal reflections
•	Changes in perception of time, self, or surroundings
•	Feelings of connection, insight, uncertainty, vulnerability, or discomfort
There is no guaranteed outcome. Every person’s experience is unique.

sections.heading: Personal Responsibility & Choice
paragraphs:
You understand that participation involves personal responsibility and informed choice.

You agree to consider your own circumstances, including physical health, emotional wellbeing, medications, personal history, environment, relationships, and available support systems when deciding whether this support is appropriate for you.

You agree to communicate any concerns that may affect your ability to participate safely and meaningfully.

sections.heading: Alternatives
paragraphs: No other medicine produces ketamine's specific effect. Psychotherapy without ketamine is available and can be effective. Depression, PTSD, and bipolar disorders are commonly treated with antidepressants, mood stabilizers, and psychotherapy; PTSD is often treated with EMDR; and ECT and TMS are used for treatment-resistant depression.

sections.heading: Confidentiality & Privacy
paragraphs:
The Integration Facilitator respects the privacy of Participants and will make reasonable efforts to maintain confidentiality.

However, confidentiality has limits. Information may need to be shared when required by law or when there is a serious concern involving immediate safety, harm, abuse, neglect, or another legally recognized exception.

Participants are also encouraged to respect the privacy of others who may be part of shared spaces or communities connected to this work.

sections.heading: Boundaries & Respect
paragraphs:
This support relationship is based on mutual respect, consent, and clear boundaries.
The Participant and Integration Facilitator agree to:
•	Communicate openly and respectfully.
•	Honor personal boundaries.
•	Avoid coercion, pressure, or dependency.
•	Maintain awareness of the responsibilities of each person within this relationship.
The Participant is always encouraged to ask questions and request clarification.
